nina_cs: Heads-up — CardinalPay hit an activation plateau last night. Their payments flow latency spiked during peak and they saw a few timed-out payment confirmations. Renewal health flag is amber; account exec wants us to propose low-risk perf improvements before next check-in (2 weeks). Thinking: int8 quant + split routing for sensitive vs non-sensitive flows, plus KV warm cache. Opinions? :eyes:

rahul_se: Agree on split routing. For sensitive transactions (payment_confirm, refund) we should keep fp16 fallback or a pinned dedicated reserve but route low-risk actions (balance_check, offers) to int8 compact. Need canary and quick rollback plan.

anya_ml: int8 gives good latency reductions but watch quality for long-context sessions (they pass full chat history sometimes). My suggested approach:
1) 3% canary for 24h targeting low-risk routes only
2) Route: payment_confirm -> dedicated/cardinalpay-v2-fp16 (pinned), refund/chargeback -> dedicated/cardinalpay-v2-fp16 (pinned), everything else -> hosted/cardinalpay-compact-int8
3) Apply prompt-compression for histories >800 tokens (summarize oldest messages client-side)
4) Enable prefix KV cache with 12h TTL for returning users
5) Add eval gate: response-embedding cosine >= 0.92 vs baseline or auto-rollback

rahul_se: Additions: batch window = 4ms for dedicated pool, max-batch-size = 8. Canary metric triggers: p99 > 450ms OR error-rate > 0.8% OR semantic drift > 1.2%. Rollback trigger immediate.

nina_cs: We should surface costs to CardinalPay: estimated token-cost reduction ~22% if int8 is applied to 70% of traffic. Will draft a short note for the renewal lead. Also setting up a joint enablement call tomorrow.

deploy-bot: Canary slot reserved on pool `ded-card-1` at 02:00 UTC. Last health check: ok. Use tag `canary/cardinalpay-0326` when deploying. :white_check_mark:

anya_ml: Example routing snippet for ops (apply as route policy):
```json
{
  "canary": 3,
  "duration_hours": 24,
  "route_rules": [
    {"match": "meta.action == 'payment_confirm'", "target": "dedicated/cardinalpay-v2-fp16", "pin": true},
    {"match": "meta.action in ['balance_check','offers','auth_preview']", "target": "hosted/cardinalpay-compact-int8"},
    {"target": "hosted/cardinalpay-compact-int8"}
  ]
}
```

ops-runbook-bot: Recommended runbook steps for canary: 1) smoke tests (payments sandbox) at t+15m, 2) traffic ramp to 3% over 10m, 3) monitor semantic-gate and infra metrics, 4) escalate to infra on p95 CPU > 80%. Logs and traces at: s3://redwood-cs/cardinalpay/canary-logs/2026-03-26.

rahul_se: I'll own the rollback playbook and perf-sim harness. Need sample request distribution (token lengths + percent by action). Nina, can you drop those in the S3 folder?

nina_cs: Uploaded distribution + sample payloads to s3://redwood-cs/cardinalpay/samples/2026-03-26. Calendar invite for joint run at 09:00 PT tomorrow with CardinalPay PM + infra. Added acceptance criteria: p99 <= 420ms on payment_confirm and error-rate <0.5% during canary.

anya_ml: I'll hook the canary pipeline to compute embedding-sim drift and token-delta. If drift >1.2% or average delta >6 tokens, alert on #eng-ml and pause routing.

nina_cs: Action items: Rahul -> rollback doc + perf tests; Anya -> canary eval hooks + prompt-compression script; Me -> customer comms + run the canary. Will post brief updates in this thread during the canary. :rocket:
